title: Sharon AI and Lambda secure GPU-backed debt funding
source_used: Sharon AI press release (PR Newswire) and Lambda press release (Business Wire, via Yahoo Finance)
key_facts: On 1 Oct 2026 Sharon AI (Nasdaq: SHAZ), an Australian AI cloud ('neocloud') company, announced its first US$356 million committed senior secured, GPU-backed debt facility at a fixed 9.95% rate, excluding fees.
It is secured against the GPUs (the chips that run AI) and their cash flows; investors include Goldman Sachs and large private credit funds; Jarden Australia was sole financial adviser and arranger.

Sharon AI calls it the first in an expected series of GPU financings for a build-out of over 68,000 Nvidia GPUs by mid-2027, and says it has raised over US$2.6 billion in debt and equity in 10 months and has customer contracts worth over US$8.8 billion.

On 1 Oct 2026 Lambda announced it closed a $1 billion investment-grade delayed-draw term loan to pay for GPU infrastructure for three committed customer deployments with two investment-grade customers.

Lambda says the loan has a 6.78% fixed rate, a final maturity of 30 May 2033, ratings of A (low) from Morningstar DBRS and Baa1 from Moody's, and was oversubscribed; J.P. Morgan was sole lead arranger.
Lambda calls it its first US fixed-rate financing and its first $1 billion-plus institutional debt financing; it follows a loan that closed on 27 Aug 2026.
The loan is secured by the GPU servers and the contracted cash flows.
quote_evidence: SharonAI Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ: SHAZ) ("Sharon AI" or the "Company"), a leading Australian Neocloud delivering trusted AI infrastructure, today announced it has entered into its inaugural US$356m committed senior secured, GPU-backed SPV debt facility priced at a fixed rate of 9.95%, excluding fees.

Lambda, Inc. ("Lambda"), the Superintelligence Cloud, today announced the closing of a $1 billion investment-grade, delayed draw term loan (the "Facility") marketed to insurance companies and fixed income investors to fund the purchase and development of GPU infrastructure supporting three committed customer deployments with two investment-grade offtakers across multiple data centers.
why_it_matters_hint: AI chips are being used as collateral for large loans tied to customer contracts.
